---
title: "Nine quadrant"
description: "Compare directional quantitative changes between two datasets or omics layers."
---

## Purpose

A nine-quadrant plot compares two effect estimates, usually log fold changes from matched contrasts. Thresholds on the x and y axes divide proteins/features into combinations such as concordant increase, concordant decrease, discordant response, or weak/no change.

## Recommended workflow

1. Prepare two result tables that share a stable feature identifier.
2. Confirm that both effect columns use the same direction convention (for example Treatment minus Control).
3. Merge only on the intended identifier.
4. Set biologically/statistically justified x- and y-axis thresholds.
5. Inspect concordant and discordant quadrants separately.
6. Export the merged classification table together with the plot.

::: {.callout-warning}
If one contrast is `A - B` and the other is `B - A`, the apparent concordance will be reversed. Always verify contrast direction before interpreting quadrants.
:::
